title: OOP & Design Basics
intro: Object-oriented design basics interview questions test whether you can think about code structure, not just write code that works. This module covers the four OOP pillars with Ruby examples (encapsulation — private methods and instance variables, abstraction — expose a clean interface, inheritance — class Dog < Animal, polymorphism — same method name different behavior), the BankAccount class design exercise interviewers use to test OOP thinking, DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) — recognising duplication and extracting a method, Keep It Simple, the Ruby naming conventions interviewers care about (predicate methods end with ?, mutating methods end with !, constants in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE), and SOLID at a concept level (single responsibility — one class, one job; open/closed — open to extension). All explanations stay at fresher depth — no service objects, no hexagonal architecture.
